analysis: Both changed files are test-only. StandaloneServerTests.swift (hunk at line 663) changes the signature of the StandaloneStubLanguageModel.prepare stub to match a new LanguageModel protocol: (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters) replaces windowSize. The stub returns .tokens(input.text) and has no crypto, authorization, network, storage or key handling. The shown tests at lines 1256-1475 are unchanged context. They cover Prometheus metrics shape and the per-model activation floor / KV grant re-slice behavior in standalone serving. These are memory-sizing availability controls, not threat-model boundaries such as TB-002/TB-007 or the T-041 cache posture. LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift changes only `import MLXLMCommon` to `@testable import MLXLMCommon` (line 3). That affects test-time visibility only and does not change production access control. The visible tests pin LaunchAgent environment passthrough allowlists, which exclude UNRELATED_SECRET, PATH and Gemma config-backed keys. Those tests are unchanged. Neither file alters production attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041), the WebSocket protocol or fan helper behavior. Remaining question for integration: the upstream MLXLMCommon LanguageModel protocol change (state/prefill parameters) sits in non-supplied production sources. Whether those sources preserve prefill/deadline and cache semantics is outside this batch and not evidenced here. No concrete security regression is identified from the supplied units.
